messages:
ashley: Heads up — eu-west3 GPU pool is seeing a spike in provisioning failures tied to local NVMe write stalls. Started when a large scratchpool backfill kicked off ~08:07 UTC. GC/cleaner activity looks correlated with GPU attach latency.
devon: saw this too. hosts showing write latency 10-30x baseline, iops starved. GPU jobs failing with "attach timeout".
ashley: pasted the top errors from node logs:

```
[2026-03-20T08:09:12Z] nvme0n1: write latency spike: avg 120ms (p95 450ms)
[2026-03-20T08:09:13Z] scrub-cleaner[1123]: concurrency=24 active=18 backlog=340
[2026-03-20T08:09:14Z] gpu-scheduler: attach timeout for pod redwood-gpu-xy (waited 180s)
```
maria: is this the usual cleaner schedule kicking off? We pushed a backfill policy yesterday to rebalance wear.
devon: yes, backfill job started at 08:05 UTC. The issue is the janitor/concurrency bumped to 24 on those nodes; that aligns with the `scrub-cleaner` backlog in the logs.
raj: quick thought — could be cgroup/io limits at container level + fio-like backfill read/write pattern causing head-of-line IO. Also saw some thermal throttling on a subset of disks (SMART temp 63C).
sre-bot: alert: eu-west3 scratchpool backfill started (job id bfill-20260320-01). Throttling heuristics engaged on 37/120 nodes.
ashley: Proposed mitigations:
- reduce janitor concurrency to 8 for scratchpool backfill (fast mitigation)
- set backfill to `io_qos=background` (so it yields to kube attach/write-reqs)
- add a temporary nation-wide attach-fallback: route GPU attaches to dedicated pool in us-west while eu-west3 heals
devon: can do concurrency change now, rolling patch to scratch-janitor config. assigning to @devon.
maria: also recommend throttling `fstrim` overlap and disable aggressive compaction during backfill. compaction was at default aggressive.
raj: for medium-term: we should add a kernel-level io scheduler tweak per scratchpool nodes and ensure we expose disk QoS to the orchestrator. Maybe add `blkio.weight` limits for backfill containers.
ashley: I'll open a short RFC for QoS exposure, but immediate action first. Devon — please post the command you'll run.
devon: running:
```
kubectl -n infra set env ds/scratch-janitor JANITOR_CONCURRENCY=8 --record
kubectl -n infra patch cm scratch-config --patch '{"io_qos":"background"}'
```
Applying now.
(devon edits applied) devon: rolled to 50% nodes, monitoring IOPS.
sre-bot: metric update: eu-west3 local-nvme write latency p95 dropped from 420ms -> 95ms on nodes with updated config (2m after rollout).
maria: GPU attach failures dropped ~70% in the last 6m. Nice.
raj: note the SMART temps — we should mark the hottest devices for a cool-off window next time backfill is scheduled. thermal increases amplify write latency non-linearly.
ashley: Agreed. Action items:
- devon: complete rollout and keep concurrency=8 until backfill finishes (in ~2h)
- maria: patch backfill job to default to io_qos=background and reduce compaction during backfill
- raj: draft kernel io scheduler + blkio proposal (short RFC) for next week
- ops-runbook: add a checkbox to detect SMART temp >60C and auto-slow backfill
devon: rolling to 100% now. will followup in 15.
sre-bot: note: attach-fallback to us-west not triggered (not needed after mitigation).
ashley: Great triage. Leaving thread open for postmortem notes — will collect metrics and put a short postmortem in /postmortems once backfill completes.
maria: uploading a sample perf snapshot to the thread after backfill completes.
raj: Thanks all. :thumbsup:
